accessibility:
- Each `Checkbox` is rendered as a `<label>` wrapping an `<input type="checkbox">` and the label text, for optimal accessibility.
- The clickable area includes both box and label by default.
- Browsers expose a box with `indeterminate` set as mixed, so the component adds no ARIA for it.
- The box is at least 24px square, the minimum size WCAG 2.2 sets for a target (2.5.8), whatever `--bulma-checkbox-size` says. [Box Size](https://bestax.io/docs/api/form/checkbox#box-size) shows how to make it smaller, and why to keep the label text inside the `Checkbox` when you do.
- An unchecked box shows only its border, `--bulma-checkbox-border-color`. It defaults to `--bulma-text-weak`, which holds the 3:1 contrast WCAG asks of a control's boundary (non-text contrast) on Bulma's page and card surfaces in light and dark. Hold a replacement border, and a custom check color on its fill, to 3:1 as well.
- In forced colors (Windows contrast themes), the box, the check mark and the mixed dash take system colors, so they stay visible whatever the variables hold.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description: Shows the mixed state, as in a "Select all" box when some of what it covers is checked. It's a look and an announcement only: `checked` is still the value, and a click still toggles `checked`. Set to `true` or `false`, it's controlled: a browser clears the mixed state on a click, so the component sets it again from this prop after every click and every render. Unset isn't `false`. The component leaves the input's own `indeterminate` property alone, so a ref can set it, and going from set to unset clears it once and hands it back. It has no HTML attribute, so server-rendered markup can't carry it, and a mixed box renders unmixed until hydration.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes, on the outer `<label>`. That's the element that declares the `--bulma-checkbox-*` variables, so a class is how to set one: `style` and the other input attributes go to the `<input>`. Name `.styled-checkbox` beside your class in the selector, so it beats the label's own declaration whatever order the stylesheets load in. A `color` prop declares the fills again on `.styled-checkbox.is-<color>`, which ties that selector, so leave `color` unset when a class sets them.
